about_the_game:
Welcome to The Neeblarium; a living ecosystem full of tiny creatures called Neeblies. They hatch, wander, form families, carve out homes, and slowly turn a blank dish into a humming little ecosystem.

I started this project during a difficult season of my life; a long stretch of waiting rooms and quiet hours where I needed something gentle to focus on. It accidentally grew into a calm little world I like having open on a second monitor while I work. My hope is that it feels that way for you too: gentle, curious, and quietly alive.

What you actually do

  • Use the dropper to place Florin to grow fertile beds that produce food and water.

  • Use the dropper to place eggs and watch Neeblies hatch and find their way.

  • Let the colony grow, eat, drink, rest, and pair off on their own.

  • Use toys to lift their mood, and superfoods when things get dire.

  • Zoom in to follow one Neeblie’s life, or zoom out and just let the world run.

You can be very hands-on, or almost completely hands-off. The simulation doesn’t need you every second; it’s happy to just… simmer.

Under the glass

Every Neeblie carries a unique genetic code that shapes:

  • Color and glow

  • Perception and speed

  • How bold, curious, or social they are

  • How long they live and how quickly they bounce back

Traits pass to offspring with small mutations, so over time your Neeblarium drifts into its own “house style” of creatures. Clans of similar colors tend to form, lineages get stranger, and sometimes you’ll see a Neeblie behave in a way you’ve never seen before and have to ask: …why did you just do that?

Very rarely, a Golden Neeblie appears — a mythic lineage with a long lifespan and a distinct glow. They’re meant to be the “anchor characters” in your world: something you protect, follow, and brag about a little.

Current Features

  • A cozy, living world: Dozens to hundreds of Neeblies, each with their own needs, mood, and tiny priorities.

  • Tray-based, diegetic UI: Everything (Florin, eggs, toys, superfoods) lives in an in-world tray you pull out and play with.

  • Emergent genetics: True inheritance and mutation across generations; no two colonies evolve the same way.

  • Lineages & families: Neeblies remember home beds, seek partners, and build up generations over time.

  • Crisis & recovery: Florin Beds can run low, moods can dip, and you can step in with resources or superfoods to stabilize the ecosystem.

  • Watch or tinker: Run it like a screensaver, or min-max your way to specific colors, behaviors, or family lines.

Coming During Early Access

I’m actively developing The Neeblarium in public. As Early Access continues, I’m aiming to add:

  • The Geneticist’s Toolkit – A cozy lab where you can design genomes with sliders, test them in a tiny side-dish, then synthesize custom eggs for your main world.

  • Deeper heritage & pedigrees – Better tools to follow specific lineages, see family trees, and track long-term histories.

  • More toys, foods, and moods – Additional ways to care for (or gently stress) your colony.

  • Quality-of-life & polish – Tutorial hints, accessibility options, more ambience, and plenty of little visual touches.

If you like artificial life toys, aquarium games, watching graphs secretly hide inside something cozy, or just want a gentle sim to keep you company while you do other things… this is the little world I’m building for you.

Thanks for taking a look,
– Ghost 🪴

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: OS: Windows 10/11 (64‑bit)
  • Processor: Intel Core i5‑6600K / AMD Ryzen 3 1200 or better
  • Memory: 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Vulkan‑capable GPU (integrated OK); 1 GB VRAM
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 500 MB available space

short_description: A cozy living ecosystem where tiny creatures evolve, form families, and build a world of their own. Watch your Neeblies grow across generations, tinker with genetics, or simply relax and let your little ecosystem thrive.
